description: Since defk-nbl each loaded library image has its own frame resource type and counters, so __defk_stats__/0 (frames_live, promotions, yields) reports only the current library. Frames still live in an upgraded-away library (a kernel suspended across a reload) are not counted. Decide: document per-library semantics in README, and/or add an aggregate across loaded images (e.g. a shared counter in a separate tiny runtime NIF or :persistent_term updated from load/unload). Add a test in test/upgrade_test.exs for whichever semantics is chosen.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Document that __defk_stats__/0 counts only the currently loaded library of a module, and test it across a hot reload

**Decision (maintainer, triage 2026-10-11):** per-library semantics, documented; no aggregate across loaded images.

**Current behavior:**
Each loaded library image has its own frame resource type and counters (defk-nbl), so after a hot code upgrade __defk_stats__/0 (frames_live, promotions, yields, ...) reports only the new library; frames still live in the old image (a kernel suspended across the reload) are not counted. This is not documented.

**Desired behavior:**
- The Defk moduledoc's generated-functions row for __defk_stats__/0 and the runtime-contract guide say the counters are per loaded library: they start at zero for a newly loaded version, and a call still running in the old version is counted there, not in the new one's stats.
- A test in the upgrade tests shows: counters of the new version start from zero after a reload, and a call suspended in the old version and finishing after the reload does not show in the new version's frames_live.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Docs updated in both places
- [ ] The upgrade test above passes reliably (run it several times)
- [ ] `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- An aggregate counter across library images

title: Define __defk_stats__ semantics across hot reloads
